Regarding the cache behavior: React applications are Single Page Applications (SPAs). When you navigate between routes (e.g., from Roster to Lore), the `Roster` component is unmounted (removed from the DOM), and the `Lore` component is mounted. This naturally fulfills the requirement of "displaying and loading the background only when opening the page" and "clearing it (removing the element) upon leaving". While the browser itself maintains a disk cache of the image file to speed up subsequent loads, the image element itself is removed from memory and the DOM when you leave the page, which aligns with standard resource management in React.
